subject: Media Literacy
title: Color Grading and Mood Manipulation
description: A 60-second lesson on Color Grading and Mood Manipulation.

hook.text: A politician's photo gets an orange tint and harsh shadows. They look unhealthy and untrustworthy. Same person, same day.

buildup.text: Color grading adjusts an image's colors, contrast, and tone to create specific emotional responses.

discovery.text: News outlets choose color grading for images — warm tones for friendly stories, cold and dark for negative ones.

twist.text: Color manipulation is rarely discussed because it's considered 'editing,' not 'altering.' But it shapes perception.

climax.text: The same photo with different color grading tells two completely different emotional stories.

punchline.text: Warm light flatters. Cold light accuses. Same face. Different filter.

quiz.question: How does color grading manipulate perception?
options: It changes what's in the photo
It adjusts colors and tone to create specific emotional responses
